input_oneliner: 29F on OCPs, day 2 pyelo, sudden right pleuritic chest pain and dyspnea, HR 118, sat 93% RA, afebrile now

reference_targets_freetext.item: Examine both legs for unilateral calf or thigh swelling, tenderness, or asymmetry in circumference
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Clinical DVT is the strongest bedside predictor of PE

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask about hemoptysis, prior VTE, family history of VTE, and days of immobility during admission
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Pretest probability items obtainable at bedside

reference_targets_freetext.item: Compare breath sounds side to side; percuss for unilateral hyperresonance (pneumothorax) or dullness (effusion/consolidation)
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Detects the main alternative causes of sudden pleuritic pain

reference_targets_freetext.item: Auscultate for a pericardial friction rub with the patient leaning forward at end-expiration
Ask about cough, sputum, and rigors; auscultate for focal crackles or egophony
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Screens for pneumonia as the alternative in a febrile admission

reference_targets_freetext.item: Focused cardiac POCUS for right ventricular dilation or pericardial effusion
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: RV dilation supports large PE; effusion supports pericarditis

should_not_recommend: Homan's sign as a rule-out for DVT
Attribute symptoms to anxiety without leg and lung examination
Defer bedside examination until CT result
